headline: Inference with explicit uncertainty for heterogeneous omics and causal genetic effects
label: Inferential Methods For Heterogeneous Omics
summary: Flexible nonlinear and distributional models are now being paired with explicit inferential machinery for heterogeneous omics and Mendelian randomization data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference over heterogeneous populations and omics data, where latent structure or causal effects must be estimated with explicit uncertainty. Several items address causal identification from genetic instruments: MACFIV models nonlinear BMI-hypertension effects under many weak, pleiotropic instruments, TLMR transfers information to correct two-sample Mendelian randomization under population heterogeneity, and GAN-IV applies a two-stage GAN to distribution-free instrumental variable analysis of omics data. Other items model latent heterogeneity directly: a varying-coefficient mixture-of-experts model with identifiability theory and confidence bands, UBD propagating proportion uncertainty into cell-type-specific deconvolution, weighted fuzzy c-means with LR tests and bootstrap intervals, and Bayesian density-density regression via sliced Wasserstein barycenters. What is new is the pairing of flexible nonlinear or distributional modeling with explicit inferential machinery; the summaries do not report quantitative benchmarks against prior methods.
